stance_summary: The FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% in July with an unusually large three-member hawkish dissent (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) pushing for an immediate hike, the most divided vote since 2016. Chair Warsh has stressed inflation is 'concerning' and unresolved, while several voters (Williams, Barr, Jefferson) have opened the door to a September hike, though Waller, Bowman and Paulson favor holding barring a hot August CPI print.
policy_outlook: September 15-16 is a live, closely contested meeting with CME FedWatch and prediction markets oscillating between roughly 50-66% odds of a 25bp hike depending on daily Fed-speak, ahead of the critical August CPI report due September 11. A strong August payrolls beat (162k) and firm 4.1% unemployment have shifted Fed attention toward above-target inflation (3.4% headline, 2.5% core as of July) rather than labor-market softness. A hawkish hold with a split SEP dot plot remains a plausible middle outcome if inflation data comes in merely in-line rather than hot.
alert: August CPI report releases September 11, 2026, one trading week before the September 15-16 FOMC decision; markets see this print as the swing factor between a third consecutive hold and the first hike of the cycle.

members.name: Kevin Warsh
members.title: Chair
members.note: Warsh avoided explicit forward guidance at Jackson Hole but called inflation 'concerning' and said softer summer readings don't show underlying trends have meaningfully improved. He has pushed the Fed toward a more minimalist, hawkish-leaning communication style since taking over in May 2026.
members.latest_source: Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium speech, August 28, 2026

members.name: Jerome Powell
members.title: Governor (former Chair)
members.note: Powell stepped down as Chair in May 2026 but remains a Board Governor, saying he intends to 'keep a low profile' and not shadow the new chair. He has largely avoided public commentary on the near-term rate path since the transition.
members.latest_source: 2026 John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award remarks

members.name: John Williams
members.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of New York; FOMC Vice Chair
members.note: Williams shifted from a 'wait-and-see' posture to explicitly signaling openness to a September hike, saying there are 'no clear signs' current policy is sufficient to return inflation to target. He called recent inflation data 'encouraging' but wants a fuller picture before committing either way.

members.name: Michael Barr
members.title: Governor
members.note: Barr said he is ready to act 'decisively to raise rates' if August inflation data comes in hot, citing risk of broader price pressures taking hold after more than five years above target. He remains formally open to either a hike or a hold pending the data.
members.latest_source: Second Chance Lending Forum remarks, September 1, 2026

members.name: Michelle Bowman
members.title: Vice Chair for Supervision
members.note: Bowman has repeatedly cautioned against hiking to offset what she views as a temporary energy-driven inflation spike, warning it would add 'unwarranted policy restraint.' She has said she's penciled in multiple rate cuts later in 2026 given ongoing labor-market fragility.
members.latest_source: Speech on monetary policy, May 29, 2026 (Reykjavík Economic Conference)

members.name: Lisa Cook
members.title: Governor
members.note: Cook has flagged core PCE running near 3.3% as too high and said she is prepared to support a rate increase if necessary, while also noting disinflationary forces could bring inflation down without further tightening. She describes the labor market as stable in a 'low-hire, low-fire' environment.
members.latest_source: Speech on the U.S. and Alaskan economies, August 28, 2026

members.name: Philip Jefferson
members.title: Vice Chair
members.note: Jefferson has warned that if inflation doesn't cool soon it 'could be appropriate to reconsider' the current policy stance to preserve credibility on price stability. He has appeared comfortable with current positioning but flagged a bias toward tightening if data disappoints.
members.latest_source: Speech on navigating economic shocks, August 5, 2026

members.name: Christopher Waller
members.title: Governor
members.note: Waller said he is leaning toward holding rates steady in September, noting recent trends 'suggest we are finally seeing some signs of disinflation,' but explicitly said he'd consider a hike if the August CPI print comes in hot. His remarks contrast with Warsh's more hawkish Jackson Hole tone.
members.latest_source: Reuters NEXT Newsmaker event remarks, September 3, 2026

members.name: Beth Hammack
members.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland
members.dissent_detail: Dissented at the July 2026 meeting, preferring a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%
members.note: Hammack was one of three dissenters at the July meeting arguing for an immediate quarter-point hike, and has warned that AI infrastructure demand is adding to inflationary pressure. She rotated onto the voting seat for 2026 and has been among the most vocal hawks on the Committee.

members.name: Neel Kashkari
members.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis
members.dissent_detail: Dissented at the July 2026 meeting, preferring a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%
members.note: Kashkari dissented in July favoring a hike and has pointed to AI data-center construction, tariff-driven goods inflation, and Middle East-linked supply disruptions as reasons prices could stay elevated. He has shifted over 2026 toward expecting a hike by year-end.

members.name: Lorie Logan
members.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas
members.dissent_detail: Dissented at the July 2026 meeting, preferring a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%
members.note: Logan has argued that with inflation persistently above target, a fed-funds rate near 4% 'isn't nearly as restrictive as you might have thought,' and was one of three dissenters pushing for a July hike. She remains among the most hawkish voices on the current Committee.

members.name: Anna Paulson
members.title: President, Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia
members.note: Paulson voted with the majority to hold in July, calling it 'not a close call' despite the 9-3 split, and estimates underlying inflation (excluding energy/tariff shocks) at 2.4-2.8%. She says rate cuts would only be appropriate after sustained progress against inflation, keeping her open-minded but centrist.
